newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE cocoa ends higher, preparing for a shortage.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE cocoa ends higher, preparing for a shortage.

text.p: LIFFE cocoa closed firmer on Tuesday as traders started pricing in a shortage.
May ended up 12 stg at 1,025 stg per tonne and July gained 13 to 1,042. May/July switches were active, with the spread steady most of the day near 16 stg.

Some traders said the structure of London's market was pointing toward a cocoa shortage because the structure has inverted, with July/December trading close to a 16 stg premium compared to a 12 stg discount last week.

In addition, they said grading figures indicated the market can deliver about 7,600 lots, but open interest in May and July pointed to demand of about 25,000 lots. If physicals stay near current levels, they said the market could see a short-squeeze.

That fear has helped buoy nearby months, traders said. They expected July, in particular, to stay firm because July short-sellers will have to decide whether to deliver cocoa to long-holders, cover or roll short positions.

Further cocoa support came from speculation of poor Ivorian mid-crop bean quality. They said the beans were expected to be mostly small and defective. A poor crop could mean less coming to terminal, which would underline expectations for a shortage.

Shortage fears are likely to keep the market firm and even move sharply higher in the next four to six weeks, traders said. Some forecast July to move up to 1,100 to 1,150 stg within the six weeks after speculative May liquidation before first notice day on April 17 in New York is completed.
As of Monday's close, CSCE May open interest stood at 7,312 contracts, down 2,244 from the previous day.

LIFFE cocoa's gap higher at the open, coupled with a strong close was constructive. May left a gap between Monday's high of 1,013 and Tuesday's low of 1,018. July left a gap between the Monday high of 1,030 and Tuesday's low of 1,034.
Total volume tallied 6,761 contracts, with little activity seen among the funds, traders said.
